questions.question: What is the main reason Bulletproofs range proofs are considered “short” compared to naive vector openings?
options: They compress length-n witness vectors into O(log n) group elements using an inner product argument
They avoid using any hash function, so the transcript is smaller
They reveal the committed value so no proof is needed
They rely on a trusted setup that allows constant-size proofs for any statement
questions.explanation: Bulletproofs use a recursive inner product argument (IPA) so the proof grows logarithmically in the witness dimension.

questions.question: In a Fiat–Shamir transformed proof, where do the verifier’s random challenges come from?
options: A hash of a transcript that commits to the statement and all prior prover messages
A fresh random value sent by the verifier after seeing the full proof
A fixed constant challenge baked into the protocol spec
A random value sampled from the prover’s RNG and included as a field element
questions.explanation: Fiat–Shamir replaces interaction by hashing a transcript to deterministically derive challenges.

questions.question: In the IPA statement proved in this lesson, what does the public group element P' represent?
options: P' = <a,G> + <b,H> + <a,b>·Q for some secret vectors a and b
P' = <a,b> alone, with no dependence on generators
P' = <G,H> alone, independent of the witness vectors
P' = a·G + b·H where a and b are public scalars
questions.explanation: P' commits to both vectors and includes a Q term to tie in the inner product.

questions.question: What do the prover’s round messages L and R capture in the recursive folding step?
options: Cross terms between low/high halves needed to keep the statement true after folding
A direct opening of the full vectors a and b (all coordinates)
The final scalars a_final and b_final computed before any folding
A proof that q is prime and the group has the right order
questions.explanation: L and R are commitments to cross terms so the verifier can account for what folding “mixes” across halves.

questions.question: Which folding update is correct for the witness vectors in one IPA round (with challenge u)?
options: a ← a_lo·u + a_hi·u^{-1} and b ← b_lo·u^{-1} + b_hi·u
a ← a_lo + a_hi and b ← b_lo + b_hi (no u needed)
a ← a_lo·u^{-1} + a_hi·u and b ← b_lo·u + b_hi·u^{-1}
a ← a_lo·u + a_hi·u and b ← b_lo·u^{-1} + b_hi·u^{-1}
questions.explanation: The asymmetric use of u and u^{-1} keeps the verification equation consistent across halves.

questions.question: Why must an IPA implementation enforce that the vector length n is a power of two (or apply deterministic padding)?
options: Because each round halves the vectors, so the recursion must terminate exactly at length 1
Because Fiat–Shamir hashing only works for powers of two
Because multiscalar multiplication is undefined for odd-length vectors
Because inverses in Z_q exist only when n is a power of two
questions.explanation: The protocol structure is a binary recursion; without padding/shape rules, prover and verifier won’t fold consistently.

questions.question: Attack scenario: the Fiat–Shamir transcript derives challenges u_j using only (L_j, R_j) but does NOT commit to the statement element P'. What goes wrong?
options: A proof can become transferable to a different statement, enabling replay/transplant attacks
The proof becomes longer than O(log n), so it no longer compresses
The verifier will always accept any proof regardless of inputs
The group order q stops being prime, invalidating scalar inverses
questions.explanation: If challenges don’t bind the statement, an attacker may rebind the same transcript-derived challenges to a different context.

questions.question: In the final verification equation, how do the round commitments (L_j, R_j) enter the check?
options: They are weighted by u_j^2 and u_j^{-2} and combined into a single multiscalar check
They are ignored; only the final scalars a_final and b_final matter
They are hashed again to produce a_final and b_final, replacing the check
They must be revealed as discrete logs of the generators to be valid
questions.explanation: Verification accounts for all folding rounds by subtracting the L/R terms with u_j^2 and u_j^{-2} weights.
